item.text: I’m reviewing the current implementation again to find the next refactor that actually improves the structure instead of just churning the file. At this point the likely target is internal complexity in the bucket storage rather than the public API.

I found a concrete cleanup: the current `Buckets` type uses parallel arrays plus a separate validation pass, which makes the internals harder to follow than they need to be. I’m collapsing that into per-bucket objects so distribution, growth, sorting, and write-back each live in one place.
The bucket internals are now object-based instead of parallel-array based. I’m adding a small test for the non-mutating path on empty input, then I’ll compile and run everything again.
I’ve finished the edit set. I’m compiling and running the demo and test harness now to verify the one-pass distribution refactor and the updated edge-case coverage.

Refactored [BucketSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSort.java:1) to simplify the internal model. The old `Buckets` implementation used parallel arrays and a separate validation pass; it now uses a `BucketSet` made of small `Bucket` objects, so growth, sorting, and write-back are each encapsulated where they belong. I also folded validation into distribution, which removes the extra pre-scan without changing behavior.

I added one more edge-case check in [BucketSortTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSortTest.java:1) to verify `sortedCopy(...)` handles empty input directly.
